sherif: Quick heads-up — ran the replay harness against the 2026-03-10 production traces after the kernel-selection change. Seeing nondeterministic token divergence and p99 latency regressions on some shards. Need a quick triage.

maria: ugh. which shards / config? can you paste the run command? :eyes:

sherif: run_replay --trace s3://prod/traces/2026-03-10 --workdir /tmp/replay-03-10 --seed 20260310 --anon=sha256 --preserve-length-dist=true --batcher=adaptive --kernel-policy=auto

alex: thanks. initial numbers?

sherif: baseline (master before kernel tweak) vs current: same trace subset (1000 sessions).
- baseline: mean=22ms, p95=110ms, p99=220ms
- current: mean=23ms, p95=125ms, p99=320ms
Also ~8% of traces show token-level divergence (first mismatch at token 10-30).

jn: divergence usually points to nondet kernel or kv-cache warmup/ordering. Any logs for kernel selection?

sherif: attaching snippets from the replay logs (trimmed):
```
[2026-03-12T14:12:01Z] session=abc123 kernel=matmul_fused_v2 selected
[2026-03-12T14:12:01Z] session=abc123 batch_size=8 seq_len=512 kv_cache_warmup=0
[2026-03-12T14:12:01Z] token=12 output_hash=0x4f2a..
[2026-03-12T14:12:01Z] token=13 output_hash=0x7c1d..
```

maria: do we have deterministic seeding for kernel-choice? I thought kernel-policy=auto used heuristics influenced by timing and micro-batching.

alex: correct — auto picks kernels based on observed seq distribution and perf profiles at runtime. That can vary with tiny timing differences introduced by batcher ordering.

claire: so ordering differences -> different kernel -> slight fp differences -> token divergence. Also kv cache warmup misses amplify since different ordering changes prefix grouping.

jn: two orthogonal issues: a) nondet kernel selection b) replay sampling not preserving micro-batching dynamics. For apples-to-apples we must reproduce request arrival interleaving + seed kernels.

infra-bot: job replay-18601 completed: 1000 sessions, 8 workers, logs at s3://infra/replays/18601/logs

sherif: agreed. Proposed short checklist to stabilize parity: 1) add a `--deterministic-kernels` flag that forces kernel policy to pick by model+seq_len+hardware seed 2) preserve per-session inter-arrival times when sampling (we already have --preserve-timing but it was off for this run) 3) ensure anonymization mapping is stable across runs (sha256 salt) 4) add an assertion that token-hash stream is identical; if not, capture first 64 tokens diff for quick triage.

maria: I can prototype #1 and #4. For kernel mapping we need a deterministic mapping table: key=(model, seq_bucket, hw_type) -> kernel_id. We can persist it to S3 and load it before replay.

alex: also worth checking kv-cache behavior: if replay reorders requests differently, many sessions won't hit cached prefixes resulting in higher total compute. We should sample warmup slices (run prefix-only warmups) to measure hit ratio.

jn: suggestion: run three experiments on same trace slice: A) current (no timing, auto kernel) B) timing preserved + auto kernel C) timing preserved + deterministic-kernel. Compare token parity and latency distributions. That should isolate ordering vs kernel nondeterminism.

claire: logging idea: include `KV_WARMUP_STATE` in the replay header per session: e.g., `warmup_hits_before/after` and `kv_cache_size`. Makes triage faster.

sherif: good. quick sample of mismatch we captured:
```
GOLD (session abc123) token12: "...and the model will"
REPLAY token12: "...and the system will"
first-diff-token=12
output_hash_gold=0x4f2a.. , output_hash_replay=0x9b3f..
```

maria: minor wording diffs can cascade, but we need to know whether these are deterministic fp diffs or logic/path differences. Kernel selection = logic diff; fp rounding = nondet but often consistent per kernel.

alex: also saw a perf regression correlated with `matmul_fused_v2` on Ampere pods: microbenchmarks show 2-4% slower for seq_len 1024 when batch_size < 4. Our adaptive batcher sometimes produces those small micro-batches for long seqs.

jn: so batching heuristics need a guard: for seq_len>512, enforce min_batch=4 or prefer kernel X which scales better for small batches. Add to deterministic mapping but keep as an override for adaptive mode.

infra-bot: note: canary replays scheduled for 2026-03-13 02:00 UTC (10% traffic equivalent).

claire: action items: maria -> proto deterministic-kernel & hash-assertion; alex -> run warmup-only experiments and collect kv hit ratios; jn -> add replay-config flags to preserve timing and interleaving; sherif -> run the A/B/C experiments and post results.

maria: will do. expect a PR by EOD with the kernel map loader + simple CLI flag.

sherif: thanks — once PR merged I'll re-run and post p95/p99 + parity counts. If parity still fails we'll capture minimal repro and add a unit test on the replay harness for that session. :thumbsup:

alex: thanks team. small note: add `--max-seq-bucket=2048` to avoid bucket weirdness when mapping.

jn: propose gating all kernel-policy changes behind a lightweight parity test in CI that replays ~500 sampled sessions and asserts <=0.5% divergence. If exceeded, block.

claire: sounds good. also add a metric to console for `replay_parity_rate` per release.

sherif: cool. closing loop here. will post results in #eng-runtime when experiments finish. :rocket:
